findings.title: Multi-source perception has no minimum Source contract
facts: The frozen activation input requires at least two clearly identified Sources even when both are synthetic or de-identified manual inputs.

The submitted contract only says authorized records, explicit user input, or a future authorized source; it does not freeze a minimum count, distinct Source identities, provenance separation, or evidence binding.
The fixed work-plus-health fixture contains values but no Source identities or rule showing which Source supports which memory, question, or advice.
The formal Gate 2 Data and Source review was relabeled as minimum usable loop, so the required source review was not actually performed.
findings.required_closure: Define at least two distinct fixed non-sensitive Source identities, their Artifact/memory mapping, authorization and freshness rules, and advice-evidence binding; then assess the formal Gate 2 Data and Source questions without renaming the gate.

findings.title: Feedback-to-understanding lifecycle is incomplete
facts: The frozen activation input separates acceptance, execution, outcome, contextual preference, and candidate long-term memory, and requires accepted, modified-accepted, rejected, ignored, delayed, question-answer, execution, and result feedback.

The submitted allowed feedback set is helpful, not applicable, skip, correct evidence, and pause/revoke; it does not define acceptance versus execution, modified acceptance, delay, question answer, actual outcome, or effectiveness.

The synthetic scenario records one same-day rest preference but does not show the required state transition from question answer to advice disposition, execution/outcome, updated understanding, and a later reconstructed decision after close/reopen.
findings.required_closure: Add a complete feedback state/identity matrix and extend the fixed scenario through question answer, advice disposition, executed/not-executed, outcome, scoped memory-candidate decision, subsequent-understanding change, and close/reopen reconstruction without overwriting the original advice.
